# reason fixtures

A synthetic stage-3/stage-4 run over **public data only**, for `tests/test_reason.py`.
The evidence store the tests copy into the run directory is `../agents/evidence/`
(MTHFR rs1801133, CFTR p.Phe508del, TP53 p.Arg175His with their gnomAD v4, Ensembl VEP
and ClinVar records; the Frosst 1995 MTHFR paper `pmid:7647779`; one public trial).

- `candidates.json` — `03_filter/candidates.json` in the writer's shape (CONTRACTS.md,
  stage 3): three candidates in priority order. `CFTR:hom` (p.Phe508del homozygous,
  the case the tests reason about), `TP53:het_single` (p.Arg175His with a depth caveat)
  and `MTHFR:hom` (a common variant kept as a decoy so BA1 can be exercised). Every
  projected column was derived from the fixture records themselves by
  `engine.agents.bundle.project_columns`; the genotype fields (`gt`, `ad`, `dp`, `gq`)
  are invented and belong to no person.
- `joined.json` — `04_rank/joined.json` in `engine.rank.run`'s shape: `CFTR:hom` ranked
  first (`exomiser_evidence_id: exomiser:CFTR`; the tests write that record into
  `04_rank/evidence`), the other two unranked, and public CF HPO terms
  (`HP:0002205`, `HP:0006528`, `HP:0012236`).

The `run_dir` fixture also seeds `05_reason/evidence/` with `../hpo/records/` — the
recorded `hpo:` records of the five public case terms (a superset of the three in
`joined.json`) — so stage 5 serves every case term from its store and never asks the
JAX ontology API; the test that removes one seeded record serves the recorded answer
(`../hpo/requests/`) through the stub `Http` and pins that only the missing term is fetched.

Literature responses come from the recorded Europe PMC fixtures in `../literature/`
(`search_page1`, `fetch_7647779`, `fetch_99999999`), served by a stub `Http` keyed on
the exact request. `candidates.json` / `joined.json` were generated by a one-off
script (`project_columns` over the three records, invented genotype fields, the
stage-4 keys `engine.rank.run` writes); regenerate them the same way against the same
records. Nothing here derives from a patient.
